messages:
ari (product): Quick sync — I sketched a proposal for a "soft-reserve surge window" for reserved pools. Goal: give reserved customers a small, low-latency burst lane without needing larger committed capacity. Think: a rechargeable credit band that can be preempted but replenishes nightly. Feedback and launch concerns?

sam (eng-runtime): interesting. do you mean a token-bucket per-tenant that draws from a global elastic buffer? implementation-wise we can do per-pool credit accounting + short-term preemptible lanes. tradeoffs: more bookkeeping, slightly higher tail p99 if buffer depleted.

priya (eng-sre): must call out preemption semantics. customers will expect consistent latency during bursts. we need clear fallback ordering and a budget for canaries. also want automatic drain + alerting when spillover hits 30% of buffer.

jamal (sales): customers keep asking for predictable burst guarantees without buying full extra GPU. this could be a sellable add-on if we can state "X seconds at Y qps". we need clear SLA language and a pricing model — maybe a monthly credit top-up + overage.

sam (eng-runtime): implementation sketch:
```
reserve_window:
  size_tokens: 1000000  # per-pool daily credits
  replenish: 03:00 UTC
  preemptible: true
  preempt_trigger: overflow_usage > 80%
  hysteresis_seconds: 90
```

hysteresis to avoid flapping; prefer 60-120s. cache eviction and KV handling: warm hot-shard for prewarmed sessions.

priya (eng-sre): launch criteria proposal:
- telemetry: credit_balance, spillover_rate, preempt_count, p50/p95/p99 latency for burst vs baseline
- canary: run behind a pilot tenant for 2 weeks with daily failure budget of <1% preempt incidents impacting tail SLO
- rollback: automatic disable per-region if preempt-driven error rate > 0.5% for 4h
- ops runbook: who to page, how to quarantine a tenant if abuses seen
please add these as requirements.

ari (product): agree on metrics. also want UX: dashboard card showing "Burst credits remaining" + an opt-in toggle at pool level. we should document expected unit economics for common workload shapes (chat short-turn vs long-compute).

jamal (sales): can we create 2 packaging tiers? "Burst Lite" (small daily credit) and "Burst Plus" (higher cap, faster replenish). customers want predictable contract language. i'll draft sample language once eng gives numbers.

sam (eng-runtime): perf note: using a small replenishing band means we can keep most of existing scheduling. main work: credit ledger (atomic increment/decrement), eviction policy, and cross-pool reclaim. estimate: 3 sprint effort (eng-runtime + infra), plus 1 sprint for metrics and rollout gating.

priya (eng-sre): ops checklist: alert thresholds, synthetic test that exercises preemption path every 12h, and dashboard for top 10 tenants by credit burn. also we should record a known-issues doc for expected degraded behavior.

ops-bot: New doc created: RFC draft linked at https://redwood.internal/docs/soft-reserve-surge-windows (permissions: product, eng-runtime, eng-sre).

ari (product): Next steps and owners: sam to own prototype (due in 3 weeks), priya to define SLOs and alerts, jamal to draft pricing options. I'll consolidate into a launch checklist and propose target GA in 10 weeks if pilot looks good. can owners confirm? :calendar: :eyes:

sam (eng-runtime): will take prototype.

priya (eng-sre): will own SLOs + runbook.

jamal (sales): will draft pricing and customer comms.

ari (product): thanks — i'll post an initial checklist by Monday and tag required reviewers.
